confirmed_findings.finding: Legacy URL.path strips trailing slash, but test matches /api/v1/ for the actual /api/v1/ endpoint. The route condition never recognizes the normalized path, does not fulfill first and silently leaves its protocol request unanswered.
evidence: Product endpoint is https://api-adservices.apple.com/api/v1/ at AnalyticsTransport.swift88.
Apple NSURL.path docs explicitly document trailing-slash stripping.
Official swift-foundation URL.swift1091 delegates legacy path; URL_Impl.swift543-558 strips trailing slashes even on non-file URLs.
Native first-attempt wait times out at231; no unexpected-route assertion in handler identifies mismatch.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Compare expected URL identity or URLComponents path/modern path(percentEncoded:false), and explicitly fail/complete unexpected routes. Add a platform URL semantic regression so tests do not silently depend on deprecated path normalization.

confirmed_findings.finding: Fixture callbacks are process-global mutable state consulted when startLoading/stopLoading execute; tests create many sessions but only reset globals at teardown, without revoking retained transports or canceling/draining sessions. Late starts/stops and retries can therefore adopt a later test or loop-iteration expectation.
evidence: session helper6-10 creates untracked ephemeral sessions.
configure323-325 replaces shared closures; startLoading329 and stopLoading330 dynamically fetch the current global callback.
Explicit status loop constructs separate still-live sessions per iteration and continues after expectation timeout.
Failed attribution tests can leave enabled reporters/tasks/retry closures alive beyond their function lifetime because callbacks retain production objects.

Native overfulfill callstack16835-16864 reaches current test closure from PrivacyURLProtocol.startLoading; no request/session identity is logged to distinguish duplicate current request from an older request adopting that closure.
confirmed_findings.certainty: Isolation defect is directly established by source. It is a strong explanation for cross-test crash/remaining timeouts, but the log lacks identity/phase traces to prove which historical task supplied the extra request.

production_assessment: No high-confidence production lease/cancellation/HTTP-acknowledgement bug is established by these logs alone. Production generation is checked under lock, revoked tracked requests reject completion, reporter token/result/retry work is lease-gated, and old provider completion cannot clear a newer activeLease by source inspection.

Transport completion invokes its user completion outside its own lock. Reporter then deliberately re-enters withLease; immediate test done callbacks use recursive same-thread lease locking. Telemetry callbacks enqueue work rather than synchronously waiting on its serial queue. No concrete lock cycle is established in reviewed paths.
Static fixture lock is released before invoking onStart/onStop, so a global registry-lock deadlock is not supported by this source.
The missing second token counter could reflect delayed utility work under runner load or fixture contamination; do not assign it to a product logic bug without an isolated identity-bound rerun.
decisive_minimal_resolution: Initially keep production code and timeout values unchanged. Correct only the endpoint matcher and make unexpected fixture requests explicit failures/completions.

Replace static current callbacks with per-session fixture identity carried in session configuration/request metadata; each protocol instance binds the fixture and start/stop handler for its own lifecycle. Status-loop sessions must not share mutable handlers.

Track all sessions and test-created transports. Revoke transports, invalidateAndCancel sessions and await their task/invalidation completion before unregistering fixture handlers; explicitly release held token providers. Retired/unknown fixture IDs fail closed through URLProtocolClient rather than falling through to real HTTP.

Serialize protocol response/stop state and enforce one-shot finished/cancelled behavior so a held response cannot deliver after cancellation. Do not hold registry locks while invoking callbacks or URLProtocolClient.
Retain overfulfillment assertions and existing tight timing expectations. Do not increase timeouts, suppress XCTest failures, or mark privacy tests passing based on restart remainder.
regression_proof_required: A tiny native URL assertion demonstrates legacy normalized path and expected endpoint comparison before running reporter test; corrected retry-wait case passes at the original2s/.3s bounds.
Deterministic fixture regression: create/hold sessionA, configure sessionB, then release/cancelA; onlyA callbacks may fire. Repeat for A created before B but startLoading delayed until afterB exists.
Retired fixture/session late-start and late-stop regression must reject without fulfilling any newer expectation and without real network fallback.

Run HTTP200/202/422/500 test alone in fresh process with per-request identity start/respond/completion checkpoints, then run full privacy class repeatedly serially in both normal and stress/reversed order.

Collect session/request/protocol-instance synthetic IDs, URL host/path/method, phase and start/stop/respond/completion counts/timestamps. Do not log real attribution tokens or arbitrary user payloads.

Only after fixture isolation passes, rerun full app+smoke suite in one successful process. If any timeout remains, trace lease generation, token-entry count and request completion for that isolated test before changing production.
